title: Extension of scalars preserves $\Dctf$
statement:
For each listed coefficient map $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$, the derived extension of scalars
$K\mapsto K_{\Lambda'}=\Lambda'_X\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_X}K$ maps $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$.

proof.text:
*Generators.* $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ is generated by shifts, finite extensions (cones) and direct summands from
objects $a_!P$, with $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ locally closed and $P$ pro-étale locally a perfect complex of
$\Lambda$-modules (a bounded complex of finite projective modules): for finite $\Lambda$ this is
[sk-lem-sf-flat-model]; for $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, $\Qlb$, where $\Dctf=\Dbc$, it is the dévissage along a
stratification with the local models of constructible complexes ([sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors]).

*Local models.* $(a_!P)_{\Lambda'}\simeq a_!(P_{\Lambda'})$, since extension of scalars commutes with extension by
zero (stalkwise, or by the projection formula $\Lambda'_X\otimes a_!(-)=a_!(a^*\Lambda'_X\otimes-)$ and
$a^*\Lambda'_X=\Lambda'_S$). Locally, $P_{\Lambda'}$ is the bounded complex of finite projective $\Lambda'$-modules
$\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda P$, which is perfect; hence $a_!(P_{\Lambda'})$ is constructible with finite Tor amplitude
over $\Lambda'$ (and, for $\Lambda'=\mathcal O_F$, derived complete, being locally a finite free complex).

*Extension.* Extension of scalars is exact, so it preserves cones and shifts, and additive, so it preserves
summands. $\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$ is thick, so it contains the image of $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$.
